title: ARTEX AI Pentest Tool: What Security Teams Need to Know
content_md: ARTEX AI has moved from a GitHub research project to the engine behind some of the fastest-moving agentic AI cyberattacks of 2026. ARTEX is an autonomous penetration testing framework that uses coordinated Large Language Model (LLM) agents to run reconnaissance, exploitation, privilege escalation and data theft with little human input. Within weeks of its first confirmed malicious use against South Korean banks, ARTEX surfaced in a Microsoft 365 supply chain operation attributed to the China-state-aligned Storm-0940 and in a global espionage push by Vapor Panda that touched more than 200 organizations. This article covers what the tool is, who is using it, how the attacks unfold, and what defenders can hunt for today. Key Takeaways Dual-use tool turned weapon: ARTEX AI is a China-developed, LLM-driven multi-agent penetration testing framework that several unrelated threat clusters have used in real intrusions since late August 2026. Largest campaign to date: CrowdStrike reports that the China-nexus group Vapor Panda ran one ARTEX controller against more than 200 organizations in at least 14 countries over 11 days starting October 17, 2026, with confirmed post-exploitation at nine.
